description: Discover the Hermes Club entry token, investigate the death of Lehmann whose bodily fluids were drained, reconstruct the victim's final vision, and uncover the smuggling organization "Hermes".

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I don't know, I just remember I fired my gun, and then someone hit me."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "You're lucky to be alive." Temporarily relieved, "Let me explain simply. The group that captured us is a smuggling ring called the Free Corps. They were ambushed by another group on the road. I took advantage of the chaos to get us both free, stole a car, and escaped."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Thank you, I don't know what to say. Let's get back to the consulate quickly!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Back my ass. Right now, you might not even be able to go to a proper hospital." Hearing this clueless request, a surge of anger rises, "The bitches at the Frankfurt station sold us out! We're being hunted across the whole city now!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew, hearing this news, doesn't even have the strength to make a sound, just lies in the back seat breathing heavily.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: After venting, feeling a bit too impulsive, adjusts the radio frequency, tone softening, "Listen to the radio yourself."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew listens to the radio for a while, gets attacked by the boss again, now completely subdued.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If you want to die, fine, I can fulfill that request anytime. But before you die, you must exhaust all your value—until this case is solved and that old bastard is brought down and executed, you can't die so easily."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player6>'s HP change:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, sir."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Attribute modification commands, supporting sub-commands as follows:

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There are some medicines, bandages, and splints I just bought in the back seat. If you know how, treat yourself first."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew struggles to sit up from the seat, leaning against the backrest, decides to give himself the simplest treatment first, wait until reaching a more stable environment to find a way to deal with it thoroughly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Offenbach is a small satellite city with a population of about 100,000. The traffic is sparse along the way, and you safely reach the headquarters safe house.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: First drive slowly around the area to check for surveillance. If none, park directly in front of the safe house, enter cautiously while maintaining vigilance, check inside for issues, then help Andrew in, and finally move some medicines and disguise supplies inside.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Rest in the safe house for a while, try to clean up, wait for the doctor to handle it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Similar to the Frankfurt safe house, the headquarters safe house is also located in an ordinary residential area, with largely similar interior decor and equipment.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I can't find a reliable underground doctor to operate on you in a place like this anytime soon."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Let me rest a bit more, then I'll have to ask for your help again."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: 8 .45 caliber pistols, silencers and ammo; 3 .45 caliber submachine guns and ammo; 3 Lee-Enfield No.4 sniper rifles and ammo; 3 grenades and 3 smoke grenades; several C4 explosives; medical supplies and equipment sufficient for minor surgery; common drugs and anesthetics.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're good at quite a few things.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Similarly, deep within the room's hidden compartment is a secret door. Passing through it leads to a secret passage that connects directly to the city's sewer system.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're good at quite a few things.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's wait for our doctor. Not sure how they're doing. If they haven't arrived here by tomorrow morning, we'll have to try to complete the mission ourselves."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Meanwhile, Gray, keeping his head down and covering his face with his collar, is almost at the location.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and are you going to gamble on that elusive chance now?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: David, who arrived in Offenbach by bus, also chose to get off first and then walk to the safe house.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Oh! God." David sees it's Alison and breathes a huge sigh of relief.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Cough, cough, that's great, you're okay too." Alison rubs her chest, walking with David towards the safe house.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: gogogo

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Thus, temporarily safe, the four of you reunite at the Offenbach safe house.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "God! How is Andrew injured like this? Let me treat him quickly." Alison uses the equipment in the safe house to treat Anderson's injuries while telling her colleagues about the conversation with the boss.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Boss, we went to stake out the police station and got beaten badly by the smuggling ring. If the smuggling ring hadn't been double-crossed, you definitely wouldn't be seeing Mr. Rabinsky and me now!" Andrew is almost crying.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thank God, you've arrived safely too. No tails on the way, right?" Seeing the teammates arrive finally brings a sigh of relief. "Andrew must have taken a bullet after I passed out, but thankfully he's not dead. I'll have to trouble you to save him."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Medicine check result:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew feels much better mentally, but still needs more rest.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: This kind of long-unused safe house certainly doesn't have any fresh fruits or vegetables, but you do manage to find a few MREs, better than nothing.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David thanks God for his temporary escape. He goes into the bathroom and starts carefully grooming himself, completely altering his appearance.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The boss said that only by solving that damn Haddin's issue do we have a chance to prove our innocence. Any good ideas, friends?" Sitting with her colleagues in the safe house finally eases Alison's tense nerves a bit.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Hair color, hairstyle, skin tone all need to be changed.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Figure out a way to add some water and cook it. With limited conditions, Andrew can only serve these things on the table.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We were discovered while staking out the anti-smuggling bureau, intercepted by a bunch of smugglers in broad daylight. Andrew crashed the car while trying to escape, didn't get away." Shrugs. "Luckily, halfway we ran into another group who started a firefight with them, that's how I had the chance to escape with Andrew."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: In short, Alison tells her colleagues all the relevant information she found, including the event at the art gallery on the 6th, emphasizing this "Algorithm of the Heart."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew decides to dye his blond hair darker, dark enough to be brownish.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David dyes his hair brown.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison cuts her hair short, concealing her feminine features to make herself look like a man.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Very reluctantly dyes hair blonde, shaves off the mustache, then uses eyebrow pencil, eyeliner, and other tools to adjust eyebrows, eyes, and the overall shape of the face.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David adjusts his Irish features, dressing up as a traditional local person.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The four of you are completely transformed.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're good at quite a few things.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Let's try them one by one.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Disguise check result:

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Disguise as a standard Germanic lad.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Disguise check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Make up into an Aryan lad!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Disguise as a brown-haired, skinny man.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Make up into a generic passerby with no distinct features.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: I've always been a West German person.jpg

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: With the help of ample cosmetics, you are completely transformed.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The story record of the Algorithm of the Heart has resumed, currently recorded text 3189.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Late on the night of July 4th, the four of you regrouped at the safe house in Offenbach.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: The thought of being forced to oppose almost everyone made Andrew feel his future was bleak.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David rubbed his temples, sighing inwardly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: In less than 24 hours, you had fallen from heaven into the abyss.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Coming to her senses, Alison felt despair welling up, but seeing her dejected colleagues, she forced herself to cheer up and encourage everyone.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What do we do tomorrow? How do we even get breakfast?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Holding his forehead in thought, frowning deeply.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're good at quite a few things.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player4 Just say we were discovered by those neo-Nazis while investigating, and then their connections in the government got us wanted. They know about the warrant and the car accident.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: What time is it now?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: 1:00 AM on July 5th. After a heated discussion, you finally reached a consensus.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David prayed incessantly to heaven, wishing none of this had happened, that he was actually lying in his bed at home and could have Irish potato cakes for breakfast in the morning.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew needs to stay and rest for a while. He's basically a dead man now.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison packs her gear, observes the nearby streets for any suspicious individuals, then leaves the house to find a public phone booth to make a call.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David keeps watch for Alison from the street corner on the other side.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Beep beep beep.... The residential area of Offenbach is very quiet late at night. Although it's midsummer, the night still carries a slight chill. Gray waits anxiously, breaking into a nervous sweat. Just as you are about to give up, the call connects.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Miss Margaret...?" Alison tentatively asks.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hello...?" The other party sounds drowsy.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sorry to disturb you so late, we're in big trouble! While investigating Haddin's whereabouts, we had a direct confrontation with those neo-Nazi forces. They used their police connections to get us wanted! Now we can only try to change the photos on our documents to protect ourselves. Could you possibly help us?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You are... Miss Gray?!"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, it's me. I know this is sudden, but we truly have nowhere else to turn..." Alison's tone is very helpless.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I heard the broadcast yesterday. It's simply unbelievable. We were discussing the Haddin issue in the afternoon, and by evening you were wanted criminals. What on earth happened in between?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "While investigating Haddin's whereabouts, we discovered this is also connected to a smuggling ring. Their network is too vast and deep. They even tried to kill us on the street several times with trucks and machine guns."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Oh! This..." After hearing your horrifying words, the voice on the other end of the line trembles a bit. After a moment of silence, Margaret lets out a long sigh. "Huff... You've been targeted by them. Changing photos... that's no small matter. What's the quality of your documents? If it's the kind issued by the West German government, there's a special anti-counterfeiting layer inside. Removing it carelessly will leave marks. If it's just ordinary identification papers, you could use a solvent to soften the adhesive layer and then reattach a similar photo."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If that's possible, it would be a huge help. Right now, the only way to clear our names is to find Haddin himself. We really do need new identities to do many things."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But I'm not sure how long it will take to get suitable documents now. The earliest would be the day after tomorrow... no, tomorrow. It's already July 5th."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We can change the photos for a couple of days first, then wait for the new blank documents. Regardless, your willingness to help is our good fortune."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Contact me tomorrow once you're ready, and I'll arrange a time with you. I don't dare pursue the Haddin matter any further. May God protect you... Oh right, it's today."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Okay, thank you again. May God protect kind people like you. Should I contact you at this number tomorrow or call your office?" Alison expresses sincere gratitude.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "This one."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I understand."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David returns at the same time.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Before sleeping, you marked all currently known locations on the map.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David adjusts his distinctive attire in the rearview mirror, confirms it's correct, and gets out of the car with Alison.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison scans the surroundings and enters the bank with David, trying to stay as inconspicuous as possible.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Come on, let's conspire loudly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bank security just glances at you briefly.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Get straight to the point, go to the safe deposit boxes to retrieve the documents.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The counter staff warmly asks if you want to make a deposit or purchase funds.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison gives a polite smile, "We're here to pick something up."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Are you making a withdrawal? For withdrawals, please present your passbook and personal identification."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "No, we were just sent to retrieve items from a safe deposit box. You know how it is, bosses always find ways to give us extra work, like sending us to the bank first thing Monday morning to pick things up," Alison pretends to be an employee complaining about her boss.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also cooperates by yawning.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Your disguise and excuse easily fool the teller. The teller and a security guard lead you through one heavy iron door after another to the underground vault. Dozens of rows of tall safe deposit cabinets stand here, each neatly containing individual boxes for different users. Beside the cabinets, there are small private rooms for clients to inspect their box contents. Since it's an anonymous safe deposit box, the bank doesn't ask for your identification, which makes you breathe a sigh of relief.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Take the items, check them, confirm they're correct, and leave.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Check the items in the private room, confirm they're fine, take them, politely thank the staff, and return to the car.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Inside are four sets of false identities and documents, including passports, driver's licenses, university work IDs, etc.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Return to the car, distribute the documents to colleagues, then go find a public phone booth to make a call.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Margaret answers the phone as promised, "Go to St. Martin's Road, number xx. Someone is waiting for you there. Don't inquire about his identity. 10,000 Marks after the job is done."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Received," Alison replies briefly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: So you drive to an inconspicuous bungalow in an alley on St. Martin's Road, which takes you a while to find.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Very efficient work, good.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: With the new documents in hand, you finally have some confidence. Alison's tense mood eases a little.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David feels a bit more at ease, thank God. Now, how are my colleagues doing? We should find a place for breakfast. And the four of us combined have less than two thousand Marks.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The story record for Algorithm of the Heart has resumed. Currently recorded text: 3458.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Last time, you four pulled off a switcheroo, giving your documents a complete update. As long as your makeup isn't seen through, you should be safe for now.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should we eat something before handling business?" Despite the terrible situation, Alison still thinks having a full breakfast will help with the day's actions.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Looks like we need to find a cheap and affordable place," David calculates the remaining money among the guys.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Probably can only buy some cheap fast food to make do. If we have time, we could also buy ingredients to cook ourselves."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You have a quick meal at a street bakery.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This made Andrew miss real food.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Since the apartment is located in Hanau on the outskirts of Frankfurt, dozens of miles farther than Offenbach, you drove for another half hour or more.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew quickly checks his attire to see if it can seamlessly blend into this environment. Sometimes standing out means danger.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "...And who are you?" The apartment manager's voice is hoarse, as if corroded by long-term smoking. He wears a greasy cotton shirt, cuffs frayed, collar open, revealing a thin, age-spotted face.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We have a friend here."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm? What's the name?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Lehmann."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: His fingers tap lightly on the desk, "You and I both know respectable people like you can't have friends here."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Everyone has some disreputable friends, for various reasons. It's really our bad luck."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Yes, and I very much like smart and generous people as friends." His fingers tap the desk again.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David thinks, based on purchasing power and living standards, how much should he give this guy to make him talk?

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew pulls out five marks from his pocket and hands it to the doorman.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He curls his lip, "No such person here, look somewhere else."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Then dinner's on me too." Andrew pulls out another five marks.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The man's dead, found on June 30th. The police came and investigated, said it was a drug overdose case closed."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "If the room hasn't been cleaned up yet, we'd like to go in and take a look." Andrew puts his hand in his pocket.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He pockets the money, leans back in his recliner, puts his feet on the table facing you, and says dismissively.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: He pulls out ten marks from his pocket.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He shamelessly pockets it again, "The police put up seals. At most, I can take you for a walk by the door."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It's fine. After you take us there, you can come down and rest."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Actually, I have the key. Taking a little care of the old friends of the deceased is not unreasonable, just...."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Take out another 10 marks, "You work hard, this is a token of respect."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It's nothing, all small matters. Lehmann's friends are our friends. It's just, as you can guess, for us to find this place, we must have had some bad luck, not exactly flush with cash. Hope it doesn't ruin our friendship."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David surveys the surroundings, assessing various escape routes if chased by police or former colleagues.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Go yourselves. Return the key when you leave." He tosses a copper key to you.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It seems fire safety here is a concern.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Taking the key, "Which floor did our friend live on?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Get out quickly, there's nothing good for us here." Whispering to colleagues.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Take people upstairs, open the door and enter.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The door to Lehmann's room is sealed with a strip marked "Criminal Police."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and are you now going to gamble on that elusive one?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: When player5 carefully lifts the seal, they find a small, dirty, sticky spot on the door, like a glue residue where something was stuck and then torn off; it hasn't been long, estimated within a week or so.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What's wrong, aren't we going in?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Nothing, something was stuck here on the door before," pointing at the spot, then continuing to carefully lift the seal.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It better be glue residue, definitely not something else..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The moment the door is pushed open, a pungent smell hits—a nauseating mix of decay and chemical odors.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew's face contorts, "Truly refreshing."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: This is a bare, empty room with a separate toilet stall, the floor covered in trash and various debris. The most noticeable thing is the mattress in the center of the room and the white chalk outline of a human figure on it.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ugh, retch—" quickly covers the nose, holds breath "This is really disgusting."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew begins examining the trash on the floor, hoping to find something useful; it's a rather arduous effort.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's only the white chalk outline of a human figure on the mattress; you can only tell it's roughly in a side-lying position.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Mountains and soil listen to your hopes; regardless of what karma and retribution, fate already slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Andrew found a "House of Solomon" promotional pamphlet.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Crouching down to look in the direction Lehmann was facing when side-lying, trying to reconstruct Lehmann's field of vision before death. Observing if there is anything noteworthy within that line of sight.
